page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top right above the text, page number at top left. Main text in one full-width block, with two centred headings "QUIS EST DECIMUS" and a title, and a catchword at the bottom right.

main_text.p: Duplicia sunt veluti, Uti possidetis interdictum, wie|h: besitzt: & Utrubi, beiderseits. Ideo autem duplicia vocantur, quia par utriusque litigatoris in his conditio est, nec quisquam præcipuè Reus vel Actor intelligitur: sed unusquisque tàm Rei quàm Actoris partes sustinet. §. tertia. inst. cod.
main_text.head: QUIS EST DECIMUS sextus Titulus?
De poena temerè litigantium. Von straffe deᵣer, welche muthwilliger weise einen gerichtlichen krieg anfangen.
Quomodo temeritas litigantium coercetur?
main_text.p: Temeritas tàm agëtium, quàm eorum, cum quibus agitur, modò pecuniaria poena, modò juris jurandi religione, modò infamiæ metu coercetur. in princ. inst. cod.
main_text.head: Quibus defertur jusjurandum?
main_text.p: Jusjurandum omnibus qui conveniuntur, ex constitutione Imperatoris defertur. Nam Reus non aliter allegationibus utitur, nisi prius juraverit, quòd putans se bona instantia uti, ad cōtradicēdum pervenit. Item Actoris quoq; calumnia coercetur. Nam etiam actor pro calumnia jurare cogitur ex Imperatoris constitutione. §. Ecce enim. inst. cod.
main_text.head: QUIS EST DECIMUS septimus Titulus?
De officio Iudicis. Von des Richters Ampt.

page.notes: The catchword "Quid" at the lower right is the first word of the next page. The black letter German text ("Von straffe ...", "Von des Richters Ampt.") is treated as a German gloss and marked with bl. The first heading block is an italic/roman title; the "Quomodo" and "Quibus" lines are italic subheads. Some letters in the original are worn and uncertain, especially in "Temeritas" and "coercetur", and in the German words; the German text is only partly legible. The line "Duplicia sunt veluti" is a continuation from the previous page. The catchword "Quid" is also printed at the right margin next to the final heading; it appears only once in the transcription as catchword. Printed text is otherwise transcribed as seen.
